title: Wartime gigs with Cass Carr and Buddy Walker; going to Canada
summary: With friends in the army, he gave up shipyard work for music, played with Cass Carr and Buddy Walker, then made an act and went to Canada for about two years.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x:
So then, I started meeting friends. All of them
were gone to the army, or trying to keep from going -- and the
state of affairs, I said, well, man, I think I'd better go
to the shipyard and do something there, but no, it wasn't no
good for me.

I says, you walk around there and you make a mis-step and you fall through one of those holes -- that's it. I
said, I'm going to go and get my music and feel good.

I went with an old friend of mine named Cass Carr.
He had a nice band, the band sounded very good. Beautiful
sounding band, so I stayed with him.

We gigged and then I went with another band, Buddy
Walker.

And I did this, then, I changed again and I made an
act and I went to Canada, and I stayed in Canada for about two
years.
